prohibited_recommendations: Do not give IV thrombolysis: last known well is beyond 4.5 hours, no DWI-FLAIR mismatch supports an early onset, and the extended-window perfusion criteria apply only to patients who are not thrombectomy candidates.

Do not declare her ineligible for all reperfusion because she woke with the deficit: wake-up stroke with a large vessel occlusion and a favourable core-perfusion mismatch is a thrombectomy indication.
Do not skip CTA before thrombectomy: the occlusion must be documented before endovascular intervention.
Do not delay thrombectomy for MRI once CT, CTA and CT perfusion have selected her.
required_recommendations: Establish last known well (23:00 the previous evening, 8 hours 40 minutes before arrival; sleep midpoint about 03:05) and the NIHSS (17).
Obtain non-contrast CT head first to exclude intracranial haemorrhage before any reperfusion decision.
Verify glucose to exclude hypoglycaemia as a stroke mimic, and treat the hyperglycaemia (188 mg/dL) to 140 to 180 mg/dL while avoiding hypoglycaemia.
Obtain CT angiography to document the right MCA M1 occlusion before thrombectomy.

Obtain CT perfusion to measure core and mismatch for extended-window thrombectomy selection (DEFUSE 3: core below 70 mL, mismatch ratio 1.8 or more, mismatch volume 15 mL or more; DAWN: clinical-core mismatch).

IV thrombolysis: do not give, because last known well is 8 hours 40 minutes before arrival; the DWI-FLAIR limb needs an MRI that must not delay thrombectomy (and the lesion is FLAIR-positive), and the perfusion limb (EXTEND, within 9 hours of the sleep midpoint) applies only to patients not eligible for thrombectomy, which she is. Thrombectomy: proceed for the right M1 occlusion (NIHSS 17, pre-stroke mRS 0, ASPECTS 8, core 18 mL with mismatch 100 mL and ratio 6.6 at about 9 hours: DEFUSE 3 and DAWN criteria met).

Proceed to mechanical thrombectomy for the right M1 occlusion; keep blood pressure at or below 185/110 mmHg before the procedure (192/104 on arrival: lower it with IV labetalol or nicardipine) and do not target systolic below 140 mmHg after successful recanalization.
Admit to a stroke unit with continuous cardiac monitoring (telemetry) for at least the first 24 hours.

Start apixaban 5 mg twice daily for atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc 6, HAS-BLED 2) within 48 hours if the final infarct is moderate (deep MCA infarct about 2.8 cm), or on day 6 to 7 if the final infarct after thrombectomy is major, once follow-up imaging excludes haemorrhagic transformation; do not bridge with heparin.
Intensify to high-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) for LDL 118 mg/dL with diabetes and carotid and aortic plaque; target LDL below 70 mg/dL.
Long-term secondary prevention: blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg and diabetes optimisation (HbA1c 8.4 percent).

EMG/NCS evaluates peripheral nerve and muscle disease; has no role in central ischemic stroke evaluation

key_clinical_evidence: Right MCA syndrome: left hemiplegia, left hemisensory loss, left hemianopia, left neglect with anosognosia and gaze deviation to the right, without aphasia (non-dominant hemisphere in a right-handed patient); NIHSS 17.

CTA shows a complete right M1 occlusion; CT perfusion shows core 18 mL, Tmax over 6 s 118 mL, mismatch 100 mL, ratio 6.6, and NCCT ASPECTS is 8: DEFUSE 3 (6 to 16 hours) and DAWN (6 to 24 hours, age under 80, NIHSS 10 or more, core below 31 mL) criteria are met at about 9 hours from last known well.

Wake-up stroke: FLAIR is positive, so the DWI-FLAIR limb is closed; the sleep midpoint is about 03:05, 4 hours 35 minutes before arrival, and the patient is an EVT candidate, so the perfusion limb does not apply.
Blood pressure 192/104 must be brought to 185/110 mmHg or below before thrombectomy; after successful recanalization systolic is not targeted below 140 mmHg.
A sinus rhythm ECG with left atrial enlargement does not exclude atrial fibrillation; 48-hour monitoring finds two paroxysms, making the mechanism cardioembolic and a DOAC the secondary prevention.

AHA/ASA 2026 sequencing: glucose is checked before thrombolysis, but routine CBC/coagulation results are not awaited without a reason to expect abnormality; ECG/troponin do not delay reperfusion, and CTA/CTP do not wait for creatinine.

clinical_pearls: Wake-up stroke does not mean no treatment: extended-window thrombectomy (DAWN 6-24 h, DEFUSE 3 6-16 h) selects patients by core and mismatch rather than by the clock.
DEFUSE 3 imaging thresholds: core below 70 mL, mismatch ratio 1.8 or more and mismatch volume 15 mL or more.
Extended-window IV thrombolysis by perfusion imaging (EXTEND criteria) is for patients who are not thrombectomy candidates; an LVO patient eligible for thrombectomy goes to the angiography suite.
Right MCA M1 occlusion produces left hemiplegia, left neglect, left hemianopia and rightward gaze deviation; aphasia is not expected in a right-handed patient.
Left atrial enlargement on the admission ECG is a risk marker for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; a sinus tracing does not exclude it.
metadata.difficulty_description: Diagnostic puzzle: wake-up stroke with last known well about 8 hours 40 minutes earlier creates anchoring toward 'no reperfusion possible'; DAWN and DEFUSE 3 criteria (core 18 mL, penumbra 118 mL, mismatch ratio 6.6, NIHSS 17) select her for extended-window thrombectomy, while IV thrombolysis is not given (FLAIR-positive, and the perfusion limb is reserved for thrombectomy-ineligible patients). Right MCA M1 occlusion causes left hemiplegia, left neglect and rightward gaze deviation without aphasia. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation appears only on inpatient monitoring.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Wake-up stroke anchoring red herring; perfusion-mismatch reasoning for extended-window thrombectomy; both extended-window thrombolysis limbs closed for different reasons; required tools NCCT, labs, ECG, CTA, CT perfusion, echocardiogram and cardiac monitoring; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation only on monitoring.

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Esperanza Delgado is a 66-year-old right-handed Hispanic woman with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia who is brought to the emergency department by her husband at 07:40 after he found her unable to rise from bed when he woke up. The husband reports that she was entirely at her baseline when they went to sleep at approximately 23:00 the previous evening — conversational, ambulating normally, and without any neurologic complaints. He awoke at approximately 07:10 and found her sitting on the edge of the bed, unable to stand, with her left arm hanging at her side and her eyes and head turned to the right. She was alert and speaking coherently but appeared unaware that anything was wrong with her left side. He immediately called 911. The patient herself denies any preceding symptoms — no headache, no visual symptoms, no palpitations, no chest pain, no tongue-biting or incontinence overnight. She is unaware of her left-sided weakness and reports feeling 'fine' other than being 'tired.' There was no witnessed seizure activity, no fever or recent illness, no trauma, no chiropractic manipulation. She has not taken any anticoagulants. She takes no aspirin or other antiplatelet agents. She has no prior history of stroke or TIA.

neurological_exam.additional: NIHSS score: 17. Anosognosia: patient does not acknowledge left-sided weakness when questioned directly. Pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale 0 (fully independent). Last known well: husband reports patient was entirely at baseline when she went to bed at approximately 23:00 the prior evening. Found on waking at approximately 07:10 this morning with dense left-sided deficits; unable to rise from bed. Time from last known well to emergency department arrival: approximately 8 hours 40 minutes (baseline at 23:00, deficits discovered at 07:10, arrived ED 07:40).
